leading_positions.synthesis: Four members name B012 (nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework) as their preferred single part, all with the same trio: Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. They share the view that it is the most influential framework for modelling and conducting monetary policy, and that these three are the most separable originators (pricing, contracts and rule, policy synthesis). They do not share confidence in the attribution. Each acknowledges that credit is diffuse (Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler, Smets). Andersson, Hassler and Teorell each name Gali as an acceptable substitute for Taylor. Friberg adds a scientific reservation about Calvo's time-dependent pricing. Several others rank B012 only as an alternative, citing the same attribution concern. This position has the most explicit first-choice support, but the number falls short of the six votes needed.

Three members prefer B007 (collateral constraints and credit cycles) with Kiyotaki and Moore only. Krusell and Strömberg each moved from a three-name proposal that included Gertler to the pair, and Boppart's file argues for the pair. Strömberg prefers it as one part of a two-part prize. The shared argument is that the two-author collateral-amplification mechanism is a clean, original, roughly three-decade-old discovery. The shared reservations are overlap with the 2022 prize (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) and weaker empirical identification of collateral channels than of the theory. Whether to widen the prize to Gertler (and Gilchrist) is raised but not adopted by any supporter. Hassler, Enflo and Friberg list B007 as an alternative.

Dreber-Almenberg, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson prefer B026 (firm heterogeneity and selection in trade) as a single part with Melitz and Helpman. Strömberg prefers B026 only as the second part of a two-part prize, crediting Melitz alone, and says he would support Melitz and Helpman if B026 stood alone. They share the view that Melitz (2003) is the originating model, that the framework has more than twenty years of firm-level confirmation, and that Redding's quantitative extensions are more derivative. Shared reservations are the uncredited parallel work of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, proximity to the 2008 trade prize, and sensitivity of welfare magnitudes to functional-form assumptions. B026 is also named as an alternative by Andersson, Boppart, Enflo, Friberg, Hassler, Krusell and Teorell; these alternatives are not counted as preferences.

Strömberg alone proposes a two-part prize: Kiyotaki and Moore (B007) and Melitz alone (B026). He acknowledges that the one-person B026 part may look like a product of the three-laureate cap and that he would prefer to name Helpman. No other member prefers a multi-part configuration. The Committee has not tested whether the B007 and B026 supporters would accept a combined award.

Enflo is the only member whose preferred part is B009 (political economics: Persson, Tabellini, Besley). She argues that it has coherent three-name credit linked through Persson, is about three decades old, and has been extended in comparative and historical work. Hjalmarsson and Teorell list B009 as an alternative. Enflo accepts a Persson-Tabellini pair as a fallback. The shared reservations are adjacency to the 2024 institutions prize and weaker identification in some cross-country constitutional estimates.

areas_of_agreement: No configuration has six explicit supporters in round 1. The explicit first-choice positions are B012 (four), B007 (three), B026 (three, plus Strömberg's partial Melitz-only part) and B009 (one).
Every member who prefers a single part proposes one prize part. Strömberg's two-part configuration is the only exception.

Members across all positions say attribution cleanliness should be kept separate from scientific merit. Several state that the number of colleagues ranking a candidate highly is not evidence of merit.
Melitz and Helpman are the pair named by every supporter of a B026 single part. Kiyotaki and Moore are the pair named by every supporter of B007 in round 1.

B012 supporters name Calvo, Taylor and Woodford, and non-supporters also describe these as the most separable originators. Several note that Taylor's rule alone would be a thin basis and that his staggered-contracts work carries more of the case.

B001 (law and finance) and B039 (technology and trade shocks) are preferred by no member. They appear only as alternatives (B001: Andersson, Dreber-Almenberg, Strömberg; B039: Fredriksson), and B001 has been downgraded for robustness and attribution concerns.
scientific_disputes: B012: Whether the New Keynesian framework's record after 2008 and in the 2021-23 inflation weakens the case. Supporters say it was modified rather than overturned. Boppart, Dreber-Almenberg and Strömberg treat the episode as unresolved. Teorell notes the shift toward heterogeneous-agent models.

B012: Friberg raises a specific scientific concern that micro price data point to state-dependent adjustment, which would qualify Calvo's time-dependent mechanism. This sits within his own preferred configuration and has not been tested by the other supporters.

B007: Whether the collateral channel is established empirically or mainly in theory and quantitative models. Boppart, Krusell, Strömberg, Friberg and Hjalmarsson all concede the identification is less clean than the mechanism.

B007 and B009: Whether the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises and the 2024 institutions prize leave enough distinct ground. Boppart and Enflo argue the mechanisms differ. Andersson, Friberg and Dreber-Almenberg count the overlap as a cost.

B026: Whether selection and reallocation across firms is a distinct advance from the 2008 new-trade-theory prize, as argued by Hjalmarsson, Fredriksson and Dreber-Almenberg. Enflo and Teorell treat it as a live concern. Welfare magnitudes also depend on functional-form assumptions such as the productivity distribution.

B001: Robustness of the legal-origins results (revised indices such as the anti-director index, contested causal reading) is the stated reason several members place it as an alternative rather than a preferred part.
attribution_disputes: B012: Eight credited names against a three-person cap. Calvo-Taylor-Woodford is the only trio named by preferring members. Gali is floated as a substitute for Taylor (Andersson, Hassler, Teorell) or for Calvo. Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are acknowledged omissions. Krusell and Strömberg count the lack of a clean cut as a reason not to prefer B012.

B007: Pair (Kiyotaki, Moore) versus a wider macro-finance award adding Gertler and possibly Gilchrist. All three supporters now propose the pair. Gertler's credit competes between B007 and B012, and the accelerator strand is linked to Bernanke's already-recognised work.

B026: Melitz and Helpman versus Melitz alone (Strömberg) versus adding Redding. Parallel contributors Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are not on the ballot entry, and Helpman's credit also appears under a trade-politics entry. Boppart, Krusell and Hassler count this as a reason to prefer other candidates or to rank B026 as an alternative.

B009: Persson, Tabellini and Besley versus a Persson-Tabellini pair. Enflo would keep Besley for the state-capacity strand and accepts the pair as a fallback. Dreber-Almenberg's opening position favoured the pair.
B001: Excluding Vishny under the three-name cap is a recorded cost for the four-author attribution.
B039: Fredriksson, who ranks it as an alternative, is unsure whether it is one discovery or two, and which three of Autor, Hanson, Dorn and Katz would carry the credit.
maturity_disputes: B012 is the oldest body of work (roughly 25 to 45 years) and is not disputed as mature. The question is whether its recent empirical performance counts as a test that should move the assessment.
B007 has about three decades of follow-up. Supporters treat the maturity as ample, and the open question is identification rather than time.
B026 has more than twenty years of firm-level testing. Supporters weigh this repeated confirmation heavily, while Krusell and Teorell point to attribution rather than maturity as the limit.
B009 is about three decades old. The open question is whether the Committee should avoid honouring a thematically close area so soon after the 2024 institutions prize.
B039 has an unresolved question of whether the task and skill-bias work and the trade-shock work are one mature discovery or two.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler) prefers B012. His file reports no collaboration with Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. He discloses co-authorship with Krusell, Boppart and Friberg and an IIES tie to Krusell and Boppart. These are disclosed, not adjudicated.

Krusell and Boppart report co-authorship with each other and with the chair, and the chair is a frequent co-author of Krusell. None of the proposed laureates is a co-author of any member in the files. Boppart and Krusell both prefer B007.

Friberg discloses research on price-setting and menu costs close to B012 (including a paper with Hassler and Ellingsen), an IO background close to B024, and a spouse who is a former prime minister. He reports no evidence that these bear on any candidate. He prefers B012.

Teorell's file withdraws an earlier statement that Persson co-authored with him, because his profile gives only the surname 'Persson'. If this is Torsten Persson, a connection to B009 (an alternative for Teorell) would be relevant. It is unresolved.

Enflo notes subject proximity between economic history and B009. Fredriksson notes field proximity to B039 and B018. Strömberg notes corporate-finance proximity to B001 and an adjunct post at Chicago Booth. Boppart notes growth and firm-dynamics proximity to B026. No member reports a personal tie to a credited candidate.
Dreber-Almenberg, Hjalmarsson and Andersson report no apparent conflicts with candidates. Andersson discloses SSE affiliations with other committee members.
questions_for_round2: B012 supporters: If the Committee must fix a trio, is the discovery the origination of nominal-rigidity mechanisms (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) or the usable policy framework (where Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler would weigh more)? Would you support Gali in place of Taylor, and what evidence from 2008 and 2021-23 would change your assessment?

B012 supporters and Friberg in particular: Does the micro evidence on state-dependent price adjustment weaken Calvo's claim enough to change the proposed names, or does it concern the framework's refinement rather than its origination?

B007 supporters: Is Kiyotaki-Moore distinct from the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises? Should the Committee state its distinctness explicitly, and is any version of a wider macro-finance award (adding Gertler, and Gilchrist if the accelerator is covered) preferable to the pair?

B026 supporters: Is Helpman or a Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum contributor the right second name beside Melitz, and does leaving out the empirical and quantitative strands make a Melitz-Helpman pair premature? Is the firm-heterogeneity advance distinct enough from the 2008 prize?

Strömberg and others: Would members who prefer B007 or B026 as a single part accept a two-part prize combining them, and would the one-person B026 part (Melitz alone) be acceptable or should Helpman be added at the cost of widening the prize?

All members: With no position near six explicit supporters, which attribution and maturity criteria should rank B012 against B007 and B026? How much weight should breadth of influence receive relative to attribution cleanliness, and which members would move their first choice if a particular dispute were resolved?

B009 and B001 proponents (Enflo, Dreber-Almenberg and Strömberg, who each list B001 or B009 positions): Which evidence on the 2024 overlap, identification and robustness would be needed to bring either candidate into direct competition with the four leading positions?
Teorell: Can the identity of 'Persson' in your profile be clarified, and does it affect how you would weigh B009 as your alternative?
summary.chair_observation: No configuration has the six explicit supporters needed for a majority. B012 has the most explicit first-choice support (four) but also the most diffuse credit. B007 and B026 have cleaner attribution but each has three supporters, with Strömberg also holding a partial B026 position. Alternatives are listed only as stated and are not counted as hidden votes. Members have already moved between openings and round 1 on attribution grounds (for example, Andersson, Krusell, Strömberg, Fredriksson, Dreber-Almenberg and Teorell). The chair prefers B012 and has disclosed this and the co-authorship ties; this summary is a process record, not a ruling.
